\section*{Appendix C. Confirmatory Studies 14--16: Statistics per Study}

For each study and for the pooled data, Table (a) gives each decider's outcome-correct actions on fault cases under $O_1$ and the stricter $O_2$, on discriminating cases and on cases with one correct action; Table (b) compares AAF (pre-specified Qwen3-8B investigator) with each comparison decider: cases only AAF got right, cases only the other got right, the Holm-adjusted exact McNemar $p$ within the pre-specified family, and the same comparison over families of related cases (sign test). A dagger marks a denominator smaller than the number of fault cases: the v1.4 fetch rule (B2-14) and the always-on agents with v1.4 authority (B3-14) were added in Studies~15 and~16 and are not available for Study~14 (for Study~14 the v1.4 fetch rule was computed post hoc on the withheld-evidence variants only). All Qwen3-8B and GPT-5.6 Luna runs are complete.

\subsection*{C.5 Low-risk releases where AAF was not $O_2$-optimal}

Descriptive analysis added after the studies (AAF, GPT-5.6 Luna investigator; identical with Qwen3-8B and with the rules alone). In each case doing nothing left no violation and the feature stayed delivered; AAF's action also left none but used more resources. Material domain under the fixed v1.4 thresholds (p95 $\geq 450$~ms, CPU saturation $\geq 85\%$, CPU-request increase). Scale is implemented as pre-registered: replicas $=\lceil r\,u/0.6\rceil$, bounded to 1--6, where $u$ is utilisation of the CPU request. The same scale recommendation was $O_2$-optimal in 14:QP-L02, 15:UP-L04, 16:SC-L04, where it removed replicas.
